articles.title: Volvo expands driving partnership with Nvidia
articles.description: STOCKHOLM — Volvo Cars is expanding its partnership with Nvidia to develop a new generation of driver-assistance and automated-driving technology, the companies said on Thursday, as carmakers race to bring increasingly advanced hands-free driving features to market. The companies said Volvo would combine its safety systems and engineering expertise with Nvidia’s artificial intelligence and computing technologies, including the Hyperion sensor, computer architecture and autonomous-driving software stack. Automakers including Mercedes-Benz, BMW and Ford have been targeting more advanced automated-driving systems, from hands-free highway driving to self-driving in limited conditions. Tesla is pushing for broader approval of its assisted-driving technology in Europe, including urban areas with an EU-wide vote possible in December. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told reporters in Stockholm that partnering with Volvo provided the chipmaker with a “tremendous opportunity” because of the automaker’s rigorous safety standards. Huang said features would be rolled out gradually. “As the car earns its trust and as Volvo becomes comfortable with the capabilities of the cars, they’ll continue to expand the services that are available. There’s no hurry, safety first,” Huang said. Besides Volvo, Nvidia has partnerships with a wide range of automakers, including Mercedes, Jaguar Land Rover and Hyundai. Volvo CEO Hakan Samuelsson said the company would take a cautious approach to deployment. “We will never let it out under conditions which we know are not safe,” Samuelsson told reporters. The technology, which Volvo ultimately expects to support hands-free driving both in urban environments and on highways, should appear in Volvo vehicles before 2030 and will be launched in multiple regions simultaneously, excluding China, Alwin Bakkenes, Volvo Cars’ head of software engineering, said. Volvo, majority-owned by China’s Geely Holding, has not chosen a pricing model yet, Bakkenes said, but features would not be limited to higher-priced models.

articles.title: South Africa Enforces Biodiversity Benefit-Sharing With Coi and San Communities
articles.description: South Africa has operationalized a benefit-sharing framework for commercial biodiversity use that formally recognizes the Coi and San communities as holders of traditional knowledge. The mechanism relies on industry-wide Benefit-Sharing Agreements, which translate the principles of the Nagoya Protocol and the country's 2004 National Environmental Management: Biodiversity Act (Nemba) into specific financial payment structures. Institutional Authority and Current Agreements The legal basis for this system is anchored in Section 2(a)(iii) of the Nemba Act, which designates the fair and equitable sharing of benefits as an explicit regulatory objective. Under Section 83(2) and the 2015 Regulations (specifically point 39(6)(a)), the Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment holds the authority to approve all such agreements.
